name: Honolulu · Oʻahu
tagline: Waikīkī, Diamond Head and the island of Oʻahu
summary: Hawaiʻi's capital wraps Waikīkī's famous beach, the volcanic crater of Diamond Head and the only royal palace on US soil. Beyond the city, Oʻahu has Pearl Harbor, the snorkelling of Hanauma Bay and the big-wave beaches of the North Shore.
seasonNote: Warm all year. April, May, September and October are quieter and cheaper; winter brings big surf to the North Shore and the peak season; summer is busy with families.
arrival: Daniel K. Inouye International Airport is about 25 minutes from Waikīkī.
gettingAround: TheBus covers the island cheaply; rent a car for the North Shore and east coast. Waikīkī is walkable.
cashTip: Cards work everywhere; Hawaiʻi is one of the most expensive US states, so budget extra.
foodTip: Poke bowls, plate lunches, malasadas, shave ice and Hawaiian kalua pig with poi.
buyTip: Aloha shirts, Kona coffee, macadamia nuts and local art.
baseArea: Waikīkī for beaches; Kailua or the North Shore for a quieter stay

items.name: Waikīkī Beach
items.summary: The famous curve of sand below Diamond Head, with gentle waves perfect for a first surf lesson.
items.expect: Busy; lessons and boards for rent all along the beach.
items.tip: Take a surf lesson in the morning, then watch the sunset hula show at Kūhiō Beach.

items.name: Diamond Head
items.summary: A short, steep hike up a volcanic crater rim to views over Waikīkī and the coast.
items.expect: Reservations required for non-residents; bring water.
items.tip: Book the first slot to hike before the heat.

items.name: Pearl Harbor and the USS Arizona Memorial
items.summary: The memorial over the sunken battleship Arizona, with museums and the battleship Missouri nearby.
items.expect: Free timed tickets for the Arizona Memorial; book ahead. No bags allowed.
items.tip: Reserve the memorial tickets online and add the Missouri.
items.why: Where the United States entered the Second World War.

items.name: Hanauma Bay
items.summary: A protected bay in a volcanic crater, with coral reef and turtles in shallow water.
items.expect: Book entry online; closed Mondays and Tuesdays; a short film first.
items.tip: Arrive at opening for calm, clear water.

items.name: ʻIolani Palace
items.summary: The palace of Hawaiʻi's last monarchs, King Kalākaua and Queen Liliʻuokalani.
items.expect: Guided or audio tours; closed Sundays and Mondays.
items.tip: Take the guided tour for the story of the kingdom's overthrow.

items.name: Bishop Museum
items.summary: Hawaiʻi's state museum of Polynesian culture and natural history, with feather cloaks and voyaging canoes.
items.expect: Allow two to three hours.
items.tip: See Hawaiian Hall's three floors.
items.why: The best place to understand Hawaiian culture.

items.name: North Shore
items.summary: Big-wave beaches like Waimea Bay and Pipeline, turtles at Laniākea, and the surf town of Haleʻiwa.
items.expect: Huge winter waves (watch from shore); calm in summer.
items.tip: Eat garlic shrimp from a Kahuku truck and shave ice in Haleʻiwa.
items.why: The surfing world's most famous coastline.
items.best: Winter for surf, summer for swimming

items.name: Leonard's Bakery
items.summary: The bakery that made Portuguese malasadas a Hawaiian classic, since 1952.
items.expect: Queues, but they move fast.
items.tip: Get them hot, plain sugar and haupia-filled.

items.name: Poke counters
items.summary: Fresh raw ahi tuna poke, sold by the pound at supermarkets and seafood counters.
items.expect: Best at lunch when it is freshest.
items.tip: Order a shoyu ahi and spicy ahi bowl.

items.name: Helena's Hawaiian Food
items.summary: A family restaurant since 1946 serving traditional Hawaiian plates.
items.expect: Small and busy; check opening days.
items.tip: Order pipikaula short ribs, kalua pig and poi.

name: New Orleans
tagline: Jazz, Creole food and the French Quarter
summary: The birthplace of jazz, with iron-balconied streets in the French Quarter, live music on Frenchmen Street, oak-lined streetcar rides through the Garden District and Creole and Cajun food like nowhere else. Mardi Gras and Jazz Fest are among the world's great parties.
seasonNote: Mardi Gras (February or March) and Jazz Fest (late April to early May) are peak. Summers are hot and humid, and hurricane season runs June to November.
arrival: Louis Armstrong International Airport is about 25 minutes from the French Quarter.
gettingAround: Walk the Quarter and Marigny; streetcars run along St. Charles Avenue and Canal Street.
cashTip: Cards work widely; carry small bills to tip street musicians.
foodTip: Beignets, gumbo, jambalaya, po'boys, crawfish in spring and Creole fine dining.
buyTip: Hot sauce, pralines, Mardi Gras masks and vintage from Magazine Street.
baseArea: French Quarter or Marigny for music; Garden District for quieter streets

items.name: French Quarter and Jackson Square
items.summary: The old city's square below St. Louis Cathedral, ringed by artists, musicians and wrought-iron balconies.
items.expect: Bourbon Street is loud at night; Royal Street is calmer.
items.tip: Walk Royal Street in the morning for galleries and street musicians.
items.why: The heart of old New Orleans.

items.name: Frenchmen Street live music
items.summary: A short street of jazz clubs with live bands every night, where locals go for music.
items.expect: Many clubs have no cover; buy a drink per set.
items.tip: Hop between clubs and tip the band.
items.why: The best live music in the city.

items.name: Preservation Hall
items.summary: A tiny hall of traditional New Orleans jazz, with short acoustic sets every night.
items.expect: Standing room for most; buy tickets ahead.
items.tip: Book a reserved seat for the early set.

items.name: Garden District and the St. Charles streetcar
items.summary: Grand antebellum mansions under oak trees, reached by the world's oldest running streetcar line.
items.expect: A residential area; Lafayette Cemetery may be closed for repairs.
items.tip: Ride the streetcar out and walk back via Magazine Street.

items.name: The National WWII Museum
items.summary: A vast, immersive museum of the Second World War, with aircraft and personal stories.
items.expect: Allow most of a day.
items.tip: See the 4D film Beyond All Boundaries.
items.why: One of the best history museums in the US.
flow: Road to Berlin, then Road to Tokyo.

items.name: Swamp tour
items.wiki: Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve
items.summary: Boardwalks and boat tours through cypress swamps with alligators and herons.
items.expect: Mosquitoes in summer.
items.tip: Walk the free Barataria boardwalk in the morning.

items.name: Café du Monde
items.summary: The 1862 coffee stand on Jackson Square serving beignets and chicory café au lait.
items.expect: Queues; cash or card; powdered sugar everywhere.
items.tip: Go late at night or early morning to skip the queue.

items.name: Commander's Palace
items.summary: A turquoise Victorian mansion serving Creole fine dining since 1893.
items.expect: Dress code; book ahead; jazz brunch at weekends.
items.tip: Go for the weekday lunch with 25-cent martinis.
flow: Turtle soup, then bread pudding soufflé.

items.name: Po'boy shops
items.summary: Neighbourhood shops serving fried shrimp, oyster and roast beef po'boys on crusty French bread.
items.expect: Casual and big portions.
items.tip: Order it 'dressed' with lettuce, tomato and mayo.
flow: Order a half to save room.

name: Boston
tagline: Revolutionary history, seafood and autumn colour
summary: One of America's oldest cities, where the Revolution began. Walk the Freedom Trail through red-brick streets, see world-class art, catch a game at Fenway, cross the river to Harvard, and eat lobster rolls and clam chowder by the harbour.
seasonNote: Late spring and autumn are best; October's foliage is peak season across New England. Winters are cold and snowy; July and August are warm and busy.
arrival: Logan Airport is 10 minutes from Downtown by the Silver Line bus or Blue Line; Amtrak arrives at South Station.
gettingAround: Compact and walkable; the 'T' subway reaches Cambridge and Fenway.
foodTip: Lobster rolls, clam chowder and oysters, cannoli in the Italian North End.
buyTip: Harvard and Red Sox merchandise, and the shops of Newbury Street.

items.name: Freedom Trail
items.summary: A 4 km red-brick line past 16 sites of the American Revolution, from Boston Common to the USS Constitution.
items.expect: Free to walk; some sites charge.
items.tip: Join a costumed guide for the first half, then explore on your own.
flow: Follow the line to Bunker Hill.

items.name: Museum of Fine Arts
items.summary: One of America's great art museums, with Impressionists, Egyptian art and American masters.
items.expect: Allow half a day.
items.tip: Pair it with the Gardner Museum nearby.

items.name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
items.summary: A Venetian-style palace around a flowering courtyard, filled with art, and the scene of the world's biggest art theft.
items.expect: Timed entry; closed Tuesdays.
items.tip: Look for the empty frames from the 1990 theft.
items.why: The most atmospheric museum in the US.

items.name: Harvard Yard and Cambridge
items.summary: The leafy heart of America's oldest university, with bookshops and cafés around Harvard Square.
items.expect: Student-led tours run daily.
items.tip: Take a student tour and rub John Harvard's shoe.
items.why: The most famous campus in the world.

items.name: Fenway Park
items.summary: The Red Sox's 1912 ballpark with the Green Monster wall, the oldest in Major League Baseball.
items.expect: Season April to October; tours year-round.
items.tip: Catch a night game or the tour.

items.name: Beacon Hill
items.summary: Gas-lit cobbled lanes of brick townhouses, including picture-perfect Acorn Street.
items.expect: Residential; quiet.
items.tip: Walk Acorn Street early, then Charles Street's cafés.

items.name: Salem
items.summary: The town of the 1692 witch trials, with a maritime museum and old houses.
items.expect: Very busy in October.
items.tip: See the Peabody Essex Museum and the House of the Seven Gables.
items.why: A dark and fascinating piece of American history.

items.name: Lobster rolls and oysters
items.summary: Buttered or mayo lobster rolls and raw oysters in the North End and harbour seafood shacks.
items.expect: Expensive; queues at the best spots.
items.tip: Try one hot with butter and one cold with mayo.

items.name: Union Oyster House
items.summary: The oldest restaurant in the United States, serving chowder and oysters since 1826.
items.expect: Historic, touristy and busy.
items.tip: Sit at the oyster bar.

items.name: North End pastry shops
items.summary: The Italian quarter's bakeries, famous for cannoli and sfogliatelle.
items.expect: Queues out the door at the famous ones.
items.tip: Compare a cannoli from two rival bakeries on Hanover Street.

name: Seattle
tagline: Pike Place, the Space Needle and mountain views
summary: A green, waterfront city between Puget Sound and the Cascade mountains. See the fish fly at Pike Place Market, ride up the Space Needle, take a ferry across the Sound, and on clear days look up at Mount Rainier.
seasonNote: July to September is dry and sunny, the peak season. The rest of the year is mild and often drizzly.
arrival: Sea-Tac Airport is 40 minutes from Downtown on the Link light rail.
gettingAround: Light rail, buses and the monorail; Downtown is walkable but hilly.
foodTip: Fresh salmon and Dungeness crab, oysters, teriyaki, and coffee everywhere.
buyTip: Smoked salmon from Pike Place, local coffee and outdoor gear.
baseArea: Downtown or Belltown near Pike Place

items.name: Pike Place Market
items.summary: A 1907 waterfront market of fish throwers, flower stalls, bakeries and the gum wall.
items.expect: Busy at midday; quieter at 8am.
items.tip: Come early to see the fish being thrown and eat your way through.
flow: Lower levels and the gum wall.

items.name: Space Needle
items.summary: The 1962 World's Fair tower with a revolving glass floor and views of mountains and the Sound.
items.expect: Timed tickets.
items.tip: Buy a combo ticket with Chihuly Garden and Glass next door.

items.name: Chihuly Garden and Glass
items.summary: Dale Chihuly's glass sculptures in galleries, a glasshouse and a garden.
items.expect: About an hour; magical in evening light.
items.tip: Visit at dusk when the garden glows.

items.name: Kerry Park
items.summary: A small hillside park with the classic view of the skyline, the Space Needle and Mount Rainier.
items.expect: Crowded at sunset.
items.tip: Come on a clear evening for Rainier glowing behind the city.
flow: Bus or walk up Queen Anne Hill.

items.name: Museum of Pop Culture
items.summary: A Frank Gehry building with galleries on Jimi Hendrix, Nirvana, science fiction and games.
items.expect: Interactive; allow two hours.
items.tip: Play instruments in the Sound Lab.

items.name: Bainbridge Island ferry
items.summary: A 35-minute ferry across Puget Sound with skyline and mountain views.
items.expect: Pay only on the way out.
items.tip: Ride at sunset and stay on deck.
items.why: The best skyline view, from the water.

items.name: Mount Rainier National Park
items.summary: The glacier-covered volcano that towers over Seattle, with wildflower meadows at Paradise.
items.expect: About 2.5 hours each way; roads close in winter; timed entry in summer.
items.tip: Hike the Skyline Trail in late July for wildflowers.

items.name: Pike Place food stalls
items.summary: Chowder, piroshky, fresh crab and doughnuts from stalls around the market.
items.expect: Queues at lunch.
items.tip: Share a crab cocktail, a chowder and a piroshky.

items.name: Ivar's Acres of Clams
items.summary: A waterfront seafood institution since 1938, famous for fish and chips and clam chowder.
items.expect: Casual; feed the gulls outside.
items.tip: Order the cod and chips at the outdoor counter.

items.name: Coffee in Capitol Hill
items.summary: The neighbourhood where Seattle's coffee culture runs deepest, with roasters and cafés on every block.
items.expect: Laid-back; laptop crowds.
items.tip: Visit the Starbucks Reserve Roastery and an independent roaster.
items.why: The city that made coffee culture global.

name: San Diego
tagline: Beaches, Balboa Park and endless sunshine
summary: California's sunniest big city, with 110 km of beaches, the gardens and museums of Balboa Park, one of the world's best zoos, sea lions at La Jolla and fish tacos everywhere.
seasonNote: Mild all year. 'May gray' and 'June gloom' bring cloudy mornings; July to September is warmest and busiest.
arrival: San Diego International Airport is 10 minutes from Downtown; Amtrak's Pacific Surfliner runs along the coast from Los Angeles.
gettingAround: The trolley covers Downtown, Old Town and the border; rent a car or bike for the beaches.
foodTip: Fish tacos, California burritos, craft beer and Mexican food in Old Town and Barrio Logan.
baseArea: Gaslamp Quarter or Little Italy for the city; La Jolla or Pacific Beach for the coast

connections.note: Amtrak Pacific Surfliner along the coast.

items.name: Balboa Park
items.summary: A huge park of Spanish Revival buildings, gardens and 17 museums.
items.expect: Gardens are free; museums charge.
items.tip: See the Botanical Building and the Japanese Friendship Garden.
items.why: One of America's great urban parks.

items.name: San Diego Zoo
items.summary: A world-famous zoo in canyons inside Balboa Park.
items.expect: Hilly; use the Skyfari aerial tram.
items.tip: Ride the guided bus tour first to get your bearings.
items.why: One of the best zoos in the world.

items.name: La Jolla Cove
items.summary: A small cove of sea lions, seals and tide pools below a clifftop village.
items.expect: Do not touch the sea lions; it can smell strong.
items.tip: Kayak the sea caves in the morning.
items.why: Wild sea life in the middle of town.

items.name: USS Midway Museum
items.summary: A huge aircraft carrier turned museum, with planes on the flight deck and veteran guides.
items.expect: Allow three hours.
items.tip: Talk to the docents, many of whom served on carriers.
items.why: The most popular museum in San Diego.

items.name: Old Town San Diego
items.wiki: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park
items.summary: The site of California's first European settlement, with adobe buildings, museums and Mexican restaurants.
items.expect: Free state park; touristy shops around.
items.tip: Stay for dinner and margaritas.

items.name: Coronado and Hotel del Coronado
items.summary: A wide sparkling beach in front of the red-roofed 1888 Victorian resort.
items.expect: Ferry or bridge from Downtown.
items.tip: Take the ferry and rent bikes on the island.
flow: Bike to the hotel and beach.

items.name: Torrey Pines
items.summary: Clifftop trails among rare pines with views over the Pacific, down to a wild beach.
items.expect: Parking fills early; no food in the reserve.
items.tip: Hike the Guy Fleming Trail, then the Beach Trail down to the sand.

items.name: Fish taco shops
items.summary: Battered fish tacos with cabbage and crema, brought up from Baja and a local staple.
items.expect: Casual taco shops by the beach.
items.tip: Order one battered and one grilled.

items.name: Liberty Public Market
items.summary: A food hall in a former naval training centre, with dozens of local vendors.
items.expect: Busy at weekends.
items.tip: Share plates from several stalls.
items.why: The city's food scene in one place.

items.name: Craft breweries
items.wiki: Beer in San Diego County, California
items.summary: San Diego has over 150 breweries; North Park has many within walking distance.
items.expect: Taprooms with food trucks.
items.tip: Order a flight to taste several.
items.why: One of America's craft beer capitals.
